title: Intake clarity for ephemeral open models and variant aliasing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see an influx of experimental/community open models that are short-lived (security/weights change, patches, or community forks). The current intake workflow assumes stable variants with a straightforward pin or soft-pin decision. This ticket clarifies the intake contract and PRD language for 'ephemeral' open models and introduces the notion of variant aliasing (user-facing names that map to runtime-compatible build variants).

Problem: Without explicit acceptance criteria for ephemeral models we are seeing: inconsistent pinning decisions, runtime incompatibilities surfaced only in production, and noisy catalog churn that complicates metric rollups (latency, failure rate). Additionally, product/docs and runtime teams disagree on whether aliasing (e.g., "santaclaus-alpha" -> weight_hash_v2) is allowed and how to represent compatibility notes.

Goal: Produce a lightweight requirements clarification and acceptance criteria that: (1) defines ephemeral model gating attributes and required metadata at intake, (2) standardizes variant aliasing semantics and display rules, and (3) enumerates runtime compatibility notes required for safe unpinned admission and automated fallback behavior. This will be used by intake reviewers and runtime engineers to make consistent decisions and power UI/console displays.

Scope (in): intake metadata schema updates, PRD text for model-team and support docs, console display guidance (alias vs canonical name), runtime contracts for fallback behaviors.
Scope (out): full automation of soft-pinning rollouts, billing changes for ephemeral variants, large-scale catalog cleanup projects (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form schema includes: is_ephemeral (boolean string), expected_lifetime_days (integer string), variant_aliases (list of strings), canonical_sha or weight_id, compatibility_notes (free text), suggested_pin_level (none|soft|strong).
A short PRD paragraph (200-350 words) is added to Model Catalog V2 describing when to mark a model ephemeral and recommended pin guidance for runtime owners.

Console UX mock: alias visual treated as metadata only (aliases do not create additional runtime routes); clicking an alias shows canonical variant, lifetime, and compatibility notes. Mock attached in attachments.

Runtime contract doc updated with clear fallback behavior for unpinned ephemeral variants: runtime must detect changed canonical weight_id and either (a) reject with specific error code + intake webhook notification, or (b) route to a pinned compatible variant if declared in compatibility_notes. Exact error codes and webhook payload example provided.
At least two downstream consumers (runtime, catalog ingestion) have reviewed and acknowledged the acceptance criteria in comments and confirmed no blocking technical gaps.
A short migration checklist for existing open models flagged as ephemeral is provided so intake reviewers can retroactively tag a small set of high-churn entries.
notes: Trade-offs: We aim to keep the intake lightweight to avoid slowing community submissions. Requiring a "expected_lifetime_days" value is helpful for tooling heuristics but is not strictly authoritative; runtime still holds final decision for pinning.
Alias design: prefer one-to-many aliasing (multiple aliases map to one canonical variant) versus many-to-many; prevents explosion of runtime routes. We document alias precedence rules in the PRD.
Risk: if maintainers do not provide canonical weight ids, ephemeral labeling will be weak. Suggest adding a validation check to intake that warns (but does not block) if weight_id missing.

Related artifacts: PRD draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MODEL/ephemeral-intake-draft, Console mock in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/model-catalog/ephemeral-mocks, Runtime fallback proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4278
